themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Several problems have no reliable answer key to check work against. So the models' first move is usually to build one: a panel of test questions, a labeled set of known cases, a group of customers who tell you the truth about themselves.
themes.evidence: Today's identity resolution answers propose recruiting consenting customers as a truth set and call accuracy claims unfalsifiable without one, echoing the standing prompt panels for answer engine optimization, the geo switchback calendar for incrementality, and the labeled agent sessions in agentic traffic.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, an ad budget, or an instruction leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or model that received it. Compliance and effect can only be estimated from outside, never proven.
themes.evidence: Consent and deletion answers say ad platform audiences and trained models cannot be inspected, identity resolution answers cite closed platforms hiding false matches, and both incrementality and answer engine optimization answers note platforms control and conceal the treatment.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what a tool will do, they build one door they own and force everything through it. Gateway, proxy, log, spending cap, kill switch, because a sent message or a spent ad budget cannot be taken back.
themes.evidence: All three models answer safe agent execution with a proxy or broker in front of every write plus hard spend and audience caps, and the same instinct shows up as expiring daily cohorts for consent, dedicated token-gated endpoints for agent traffic, and one absolute contact limit for journey orchestration.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: Some of the hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and implied claims, and no rule set captures that. The models keep concluding that judgment can only be narrowed to a smaller, safer box, not automated away.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers all start by mining past legal rejections to lock down approved claims, while naming the judgment of whether copy even makes a claim as the part software cannot defend in an audit; the semantic layer answers say the same about context-dependent meaning.

themes.name: Politics, Not Plumbing
themes.plain: Several problems look like missing technology but are really fights over money, ownership, and reported numbers. Teams and platforms disagree on purpose, so no schema or standard can settle whose number has to change.
themes.evidence: Semantic context layer answers call standardizing the meaning of active customer a political settlement in a data modeling costume, journey orchestration answers say no neutral party can price a customer's attention and channel owners resist doing nothing, and agent traffic answers hinge on incentives for honest disclosure.
